post.summary: Finish the active search and start a new one
post.description: Archives the active search named by searchId with its outcome and starts a new active search titled Мій пошук, in one transaction, so the board starts empty. openApplications decides the applications still in applied, screening, tech_interview, final: move takes them with their whole history into the new search (one application.updated each), withdraw closes each with a withdrawn stage event (one application.stage_changed each). Offers and closed applications stay in the finished search, which stays readable by its searchId. The user's own searchId that is no longer active (a repeat, or the loser of two concurrent finishes) answers 409 'The search is already finished'; another user's or a missing searchId answers 404.

requestBody.description: The search being finished, its outcome and the choice for its open applications.

200.description: The finished search and the new active search with their totals

They never block the create.

get.summary: List Applications as cards
get.description: Filters are comma lists (stage, source, silence), q searches company, position, stack, vacancy text and notes by word prefix in web search syntax (quotes, or, -), hasScore is true or false. salaryFrom is a whole amount that keeps applications whose salaryMax reaches it, or whose salaryMin does when salaryMax is empty; applications without a salary drop out and currencies are not converted. Without searchId only the active search is read. sort=relevance orders by rank and needs q, and its cursor pages only that sort. With q each item carries snippet, the matched words of its stack, vacancy text and notes, or null when only company or position matched; without q snippet is null. Pages follow nextCursor until it is null; another user's searchId answers 404.

get.summary: Read the Match Score breakdown of an Application
get.description: The latest done match of the Application against the resume version linked to it now. The model maps each vacancy requirement as full, partial or missing with a weight of must, nice or mentioned; the score is computed in code: must is worth 3 points, nice 1, mentioned 0, and each must or nice requirement loses its share of 100 by its missing coverage, so the score is 100 minus the listed losses. The match settle step writes match_score only for the version still linked. match is null with no linked resume version, before a match is done for that version, or after the AI results are deleted. Read only.

200.description: The Match Score breakdown, or null

get.summary: The scheduled events and follow-up reminders in a range, shaped for FullCalendar
get.description: from and to carry Z or an offset, to is later than from and at most 62 days on. An event is included when it overlaps [from, to) and is planned or done; start and end are UTC. A follow-up is an all-day item dated in the time zone of the user's settings. A planned event and a follow-up are left out while their application's stage is one of rejected, ghosted, withdrawn and come back when it reopens (an undo, a late reply); a done event always stays.

post.summary: Create a resume version from a confirmed upload
post.description: Checks the pending upload again and copies it to the version's own key only while it is still the file checked; a file written again since answers 409. The first version creates the user's resume, each next one takes the next number, and one upload makes one version: a second create from it answers 409. A resume_parse AI job and a resume.version_uploaded event are written in the same transaction; the worker extracts the text and builds the AI skills profile, so the version starts with aiProfileStatus queued.

schema.description: One key per submit, kept on its retries, 1 to 255 characters. The same key with the same request within 24 hours answers the first reply again and creates nothing; with another request, or while the first one still runs, it answers 409 with type idempotency_conflict. A request that fails keeps nothing, so its retry runs again.

post.summary: Parse a draft again
post.description: Queues a new vacancy parse of the text the draft keeps, in one transaction with the application.capture_requested event, and records no second captured timeline row. While a parse of the draft is queued or processing it answers that job and stores nothing, so a double click follows one job. Answers 409 for an Application that is not a draft ("Application is not a draft"), for a draft the parse has already filled ("Vacancy is already parsed") and for a draft without text ("Draft has no vacancy text"). A text whose parse named no company and no position is answered from the stored result and fails again without an AI call. Counts against the same hourly limit as POST /capture/paste.

post.summary: Issue a one-time ticket for the live stream
post.description: EventSource cannot send an Authorization header, so the client asks for a ticket with its access token and opens the stream with the ticket. LiveTicketsService.issue stores only the SHA-256 of the ticket in Redis for 30 s, and the first stream that presents it deletes it. A capture token answers 403. Answers 503 while Redis is not reachable; the client then polls GET /jobs/{id} every 2000 ms.

get.summary: Live updates of the signed-in user as Server-Sent Events
get.description: Takes the ticket that LiveTicketsService.issue wrote, not an access token. Pushes job.updated, application.updated, notification.created of the ticket's user, each with a uuid id, the event name and a JSON data line: job.updated carries the job status without queue and totalSteps, application.updated carries applicationId and the changed fields, notification.created carries notificationId. A comment line ": heartbeat" follows every 25 s and carries no id. The server ends the stream after 900 s, on shutdown and when Redis stops answering; the client asks for a new ticket, reconnects and refetches, because Last-Event-ID is not replayed. A missing, unknown, used or expired ticket answers 401, Redis out of reach answers 503. The route is outside RateLimitInterceptor: every open follows the rate limited POST /events/ticket.

schema.description: The ticket from POST /events/ticket, written by LiveTicketsService.issue. It opens one stream once.
